title: Set 61

sentences.ko: 내가 너 맨날 끌고 가던 그 샌드위치집 알지? 지난주에 다시 가 봤는데 만드는 사람이 바뀌었더라고. 그래서 고기는 반인데 1달러를 더 받아. 그 동네에 갈 일이 있으면 거기서 먹긴 하겠지만, 그거 먹자고 시내를 가로질러 가지는 않을 거야.
sentences.text: You know that sandwich place I used to drag you to? I went back last week and it's a different guy making them now, so it's half the meat for a dollar more. I'd still eat there if I was already over that way, but I'm not driving across town for it anymore.

alts.text: Remember that sandwich spot I always dragged you to? I went back last week and there's a different guy making them now, so it's half the meat for a dollar more. I'd still grab one if I was already over that way, but I'm not driving across town for it anymore.

Do you remember the sandwich shop I used to insist on taking you to? I returned last week and a different person is preparing them now, so it is half the meat for a dollar more. I would still eat there if I were already in that area, but I am no longer willing to drive across town for it.

sentences.note: **drag you to** 는 상대는 별로 안 내키는데 억지로 데려간다는 뜻입니다. **half the meat for a dollar more** 처럼 양과 값을 나란히 붙여 말하면 손해 본 느낌이 한 번에 전해집니다.

sentences.ko: 토요일에 머리를 잘랐는데 팁 빼고 40달러였어. 몇 년째 같은 사람이 똑같이 자르는 건데 말이야. 아무 말도 안 했어. 뭐 어쩌겠어, 가위 들고 있는 사람이랑 싸워? 그냥 6주에 한 번으로 늘려 볼까 해.
sentences.text: I got my hair cut Saturday and it was forty dollars before the tip, and it's the same guy doing the same thing he's done for years. I didn't say anything, because what am I going to do, argue about it while he's holding the scissors? I'm just going to start stretching it out to six weeks.

alts.text: Forty bucks for a haircut Saturday, before the tip, and it's the same guy doing the exact same thing he's done for years. I didn't say anything, cause what am I gonna do, argue about it while he's holding the scissors? I'm just gonna start stretching it out to six weeks.

I had my hair cut on Saturday and it came to forty dollars before the tip, and it is the same barber doing the same thing he has done for years. I did not say anything, because what was I to do, argue about it while he was holding the scissors? I am simply going to begin stretching it out to six weeks.

sentences.note: **what am I going to do** 는 방법을 묻는 게 아니라 달리 어쩔 도리가 없다는 뜻의 되묻기입니다. **stretching it out to six weeks** 는 하던 간격을 6주까지 늘려 잡는다는 말입니다.

sentences.ko: 우리 팀에 하루 종일 일을 붙들고 있다가 4시 50분에 나한테 넘기는 사람이 있어. 퇴근 전에 잠깐만 봐 줄 수 있냐면서. 근데 한 번도 잠깐인 적이 없어! 그 사람은 가고 남아 있는 건 나야. 그래서 아침에 답하는 걸로 바꿔 봤더니, 이번엔 내 자리에 와서 서 있어. 그러니까 어쩌다 보니 이제 내가 문제인 거지.
sentences.text: There's a guy on my team who sits on stuff all day and then sends it to me at ten to five asking if I can take a quick look before he heads out. And it's never quick! Then he's gone and I'm the one still sitting there. I tried just answering him in the morning instead, but then he comes and stands by my desk, so now somehow I'm the problem.

alts.text: This guy on my team sits on stuff all day and then dumps it on me at ten to five asking if I can take a quick look before he takes off. And it's never quick! Then he's out the door and I'm the one still sitting there. I tried just getting back to him in the morning instead, but then he comes and stands by my desk, so now somehow I'm the problem.

There is a colleague on my team who holds on to things all day and then sends them to me at ten minutes to five, asking whether I can take a quick look before he leaves. It is never quick. He then departs and I am the one still sitting there. I tried responding to him in the morning instead, but he comes and stands beside my desk, so now somehow I am the problem.

sentences.note: **sits on stuff** 는 처리하지 않고 붙들고만 있다는 뜻입니다. 시간을 말하는 **ten to five** 는 5시 10분 전, 그러니까 4시 50분입니다.
sentences.situation: 회사 사람 때문에 짜증난 걸 친구한테 털어놓기

sentences.ko: 경기가 몇 시에 시작하는지만 보려고 유튜브를 열었거든. 그랬더니 어떤 사람이 차로 아이슬란드를 횡단하고 있고, 그다음엔 비행기가 왜 추락하는지 40분짜리가 나오고. 정신 차려 보니 새벽 1시인데 6시에는 일어나야 돼. 나중엔 재미있지도 않았어. 그냥 계속 본 거야.
sentences.text: I only opened YouTube to check what time the game started, and then it's some guy driving across Iceland, and then it's forty minutes on why planes crash. Next thing I know it's one in the morning and I have to be up at six. And I wasn't even enjoying it by the end, I just kept going.

alts.text: All I did was open YouTube to see what time the game started, and then it's some guy driving across Iceland, and then it's forty minutes on why planes crash. Next thing I know it's one in the morning and I gotta be up at six. And I wasn't even into it by the end, I just kept going.

I opened YouTube only to check what time the game began, and then there was a man driving across Iceland, and then forty minutes on why planes crash. Before I realized it, it was one in the morning and I had to be up at six. I was not even enjoying it by the end. I simply kept going.

sentences.note: **Next thing I know** 는 사이가 통째로 날아가고 어느새 그렇게 돼 있더라는 뜻입니다. 시간 가는 줄 몰랐다고 할 때 자주 씁니다.
sentences.situation: 유튜브 보다가 시간 다 날린 얘기

sentences.ko: 모퉁이에 있는 그 가게에서 댄을 만나기로 했는데, 테이블마다 노트북이 놓여 있고 누가 한 시간 전에 다 마신 컵이 그대로 있더라. 그래서 주문해 놓고 결국 창가 좁은 선반에 서서 마셨어. 기차 기다리는 사람들처럼. 댄이 갈 때쯤엔 허리가 끊어질 것 같았어. 솔직히 그냥 차에 앉아 있을 걸 그랬어.
sentences.text: I was meeting Dan at that place on the corner and every table had a laptop on it and a cup somebody finished an hour ago. So we ordered and ended up standing at that little shelf by the window like we were waiting for a train. My back was killing me by the time he left, and honestly we should have just sat in the car.

alts.text: Met up with Dan at that place on the corner and every table had a laptop on it and a cup somebody finished an hour ago. So we ordered and wound up standing at that little shelf by the window like we were waiting for a train. My back was killing me by the time he took off, and honestly we should've just sat in the car.

I was meeting Dan at the cafe on the corner, and every table had a laptop on it and a cup someone had finished an hour earlier. We ordered and ended up standing at the narrow shelf by the window as though we were waiting for a train. My back was aching terribly by the time he left, and frankly we should have simply sat in the car.

sentences.note: **My back was killing me** 는 허리가 아파 죽겠다는 말입니다. 몸 어디든 넣어 쓸 수 있습니다. **ended up standing** 은 그럴 생각은 없었는데 결국 그렇게 됐다는 뜻입니다.

reviewed: 1번 formal 의 "so there is half the meat for a dollar more" 가 영어로 어색해서 "so it is half the meat for a dollar more" 로 고쳤습니다. there is 로는 값과 양을 나란히 붙이는 말이 성립하지 않습니다.
4번 한국어의 "게임"은 비디오 게임으로 읽혀서 "경기"로 고쳤습니다. 영어의 the game 은 스포츠 경기 중계를 가리킵니다.
